c.tagline: Azerbaijani heart of Iran, home to the world's largest covered bazaar.

taxi.fareNote: Ride-hailing apps Snapp and Tapsi are cheap and widely used but need an Iranian phone number and rial payment. Foreign bank and credit cards do NOT work anywhere in Iran, so bring cash (US dollars or euros) to exchange for rials and carry cash for taxis and shared taxis (savari).

emergency.note: 110 is police, 115 the emergency medical / ambulance service, and 125 is the fire brigade.

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpockets in the crowded Grand Bazaar and agree taxi fares before setting off.

hood_desc: The historic centre around the UNESCO-listed Grand Bazaar of Tabriz - the world's largest covered bazaar - plus the Jameh Mosque and the Blue Mosque; the essential sightseeing base, dense with caravanserais and rug merchants.

An upscale southeastern district built around the historic El Goli (Shah Goli) park and its lake pavilion, with leafy streets, higher-end hotels, and restaurants; calm, scenic, and popular with families.
Tabriz's modern uptown of cafes, restaurants, shopping streets, and cinemas; the liveliest area for dining and going out (Iranian-style, no alcohol), well served by taxis and the metro.
A central, busy junction district near the university and the Blue Mosque, with mid-range hotels, bookshops, and cafes; a convenient, well-connected base close to the main sights.
A newer residential district on the northeastern hills with modern apartment blocks, parks, and quiet streets; a calm local neighborhood away from the tourist core.

water.note: Tap water in Tabriz is generally safe to drink, though bottled water is cheap and widely used.

transit.pay: Buses, BRT and the metro use a rechargeable transit smart card tapped on entry; single tickets are limited. Fares are extremely cheap. Shared taxis (savari) running fixed routes are paid in cash per seat, and alcohol-free by law.
transit.hours: The metro and buses run roughly 6am-10pm; there is no overnight service, so late trips rely on taxis or ride-hailing.
transit.note: Tabriz was the first Iranian city outside Tehran to open a metro; Line 1 is running with further lines under construction. Shared taxis remain the most common way to get around.

train: Tabriz Railway Station - domestic services to Tehran, Mashhad and Jolfa, plus a seasonal international line toward Van, Turkey
bus: Tabriz Central Bus Terminal - intercity coaches across Iran and to Turkey and Armenia

airport.name: Tabriz International Airport (TBZ)
rentals: Local rental agencies (no major international brands; foreign cards not accepted)

transit.m: Snapp/Tapsi or agency taxi to the centre (15-20 min)
City bus toward the centre (no direct metro link to the terminal)

tip.r: Not customary; rounding up or leaving small change for good service is appreciated. Note 'taarof' - a host may at first refuse payment out of politeness, so insist gently.
